The opening of the collection introduces Andrew Jackson's first State of the Union address delivered on December 8, 1829. In this address, he expresses his gratitude for the peace and prosperity of the nation while outlining issues related to foreign relations, particularly with England, France, and Spain. Jackson highlights the importance of maintaining peace and progress, discusses negotiating unsettled matters with these nations, and emphasizes the need for a constitutional amendment concerning the election of the President and Vice-President.
